newsitem.title: USA: Tour leg sees moderate scab pressure in DNS wheat.
newsitem.headline: Tour leg sees moderate scab pressure in DNS wheat.

text.p: Participants on one leg of the annual Wheat Quality Council-organized spring wheat tour saw moderate presence of scab in dark northern spring wheat Tuesday, the first full day of the tour.

After taking 10 measurements in three fields in Cass County in east-central North Dakota, the group calculated an average yield potential of 43.847 bushels per acre. But after factoring in the estimated damage from scab, the yield potential was lowered to 40.24 bushels per acre.
Last year, the same tour leg averaged a yield potential on the first day of 29 bushels per acre.

In the first field in which they stopped, the tour members estimated scab had affected around 20 percent of the spring wheat heads. The second field in which they stopped had virtually no scab pressure, but the third field had between seven and 10 percent scab infestation.
Ron Killoran, elevator manager for Buffalo Farm Supply in Cass County, said scab was a definite problem this year.
"This was a 50 to 60 bushel crop," Killoran said as he stood in a field about a mile from his elevator. "But now it's a 35 to 40 bushel crop because of the scab."

Killoran estimated that the field would be harvested in seven to 10 days. He said that particular field had been planted during the first week in May, and that scab had only become evident over the last three weeks.

The tour kicked off Tuesday morning in Fargo, N.D., and will cover 90 percent of the wheat producing counties in North Dakota. Tour members will also pass through wheat growing regions of South Dakota and Minnesota.
The tour wraps up in Fargo Thursday afternoon, when participants will issue an average yield potential estimate for the three-state area.
